colors.name: ground
colors.role: the stage — pure black ground; type is the only thing lit

colors.name: ink
colors.role: primary text and the resting wordmark — 20.1:1 on ground (AAA)

colors.name: ink-dim
colors.role: secondary text: Korean glosses, track durations, channel labels — 6.9:1 on ground (AA+)

colors.name: ink-faint
colors.role: decorative only: hairline rules, dimmed marquee bands, waveform grid — never carries meaning

colors.name: acid
colors.role: the one accent — focus ring, ::selection, the wordmark's overdriven state, the scrub playhead, the acid pulse band. 17.8:1 on ground clears AA normal text, but it is held for display type, marks, and inverted text on acid panels rather than body copy, because the whole page commits to one electric event

colors.name: panel
colors.role: lifted dark surfaces: the scrub stage surround, the tracklist rows, the footer field — keeps the page from being a single flat black while staying inside the committed palette. ink reads 11.7:1 and acid reads 16.3:1 on it

colors.name: ink-on-acid
colors.role: inverted text on acid fills — the marquee's acid band, the pressed focus chip — 17.8:1 on the acid (the reverse of acid on ground)

fonts.role: the synthesizer — variable font with width (wdth 62–125) and weight (wght 100–900) axes; the width axis is the entire kinetic premise, the wordmark scrubs and stretches along it
the Korean drum — every Hangul display glyph; the heavy blocky mass that the wordmark translates into at full width
Korean body and caption voice — prose, track titles, footer copy; Korean never falls through to a Latin sans
the patch sheet — BPM, timecodes, track numbers, channel strips; the engineer's pencil

texture: None. The texture is the type itself: a fixed 8-row grid of faint acid hairlines in the scrub stage reads as a spectrum-analyzer baseline, and a 1px acid rule under the hero wordmark behaves like a waveform's zero-crossing. No images, no feTurbulence grain — the kinetic letterforms ARE the surface. Everything else is flat committed color.

motion.name: ease-wave
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1) — fast out, long settle; type overshoots nothing, it resolves like a note decaying

motion.name: ease-scrub
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) — the scrub's lerp frame; mass that trails the wheel

motion.name: wdth-scrub
motion.value: font-variation-settings 'wdth' 62 → 125 over scroll progress 0 → 1, lerp-smoothed at 0.14/frame; the wordmark morphs through its whole range like a timeline sweeping a filter

motion.name: vel-stretch
motion.value: per-glyph scaleX(1 + velocity·0.18), velocity decayed at 0.86/frame; the faster you scroll, the more the glyphs stretch — amplitude written into the type

motion.name: char-rise
motion.value: 640ms ease-wave per glyph, translateY(0.32em)→0 + opacity 0→1, 45ms stagger; backwards fill so the pre-state is invisible only while JS runs

motion.name: acid-pulse
motion.value: 2.4s ease-in-out infinite alternate, opacity 0.55 → 1 on the scrub playhead; a held beat, not a flicker

motion.name: marquee-l
motion.value: linear, 38s, translateX(-50%); the top lyric band scrolls left at resting tempo

motion.name: marquee-r
motion.value: linear, 30s, translateX(-50%) reverse; the middle band scrolls right, faster — crossed speeds read as counterpoint

motion.name: marquee-acid
motion.value: linear, 22s, translateX(-50%); the acid credits band is the fastest and the loudest
